newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares ended well up on Thursday at a third successive record closing high and only a fraction off an all-time high set late as the Dow rallied.
Strong bonds and continued buying interest ahead of Friday's January options contract expiry helped lift the market, dealers said, but overall sentiment was also very positive.
"It is another good move, over five points, and there's not really one thing you can put your finger on to explain it -- people are just keen to buy," one trader said.
The AEX index closed at 669.55, up 1.19 percent, easily beating Wednesday's prior life high of 664.47.
The index lost ground at the open, but quickly came back to break through the top its trend channel at 665, dealers said, sparking a gallop into uncharted territory by the midsession.
A rallying Dow lifted the AEX to a fresh all-time peak at 669.57 seconds before the close.
Financials continued their good run with Fortis the standout, advancing as investors digested a capital increase at its Belgian unit and plans to up its stake in Belgian bank ASLK.
Transport firm Nedlloyd booked solid gains, which one dealer attributed to bargain-hunting and another to its inclusion in Kleinwort Benson's model European portfolio.

Software firm Baan had another storming day, adding a fresh 7.55 percent gain to a rise of 13 percent in the previous five days. Salomon Brothers upped Baan to a buy on Wednesday, adding it expected excellent fourth quarter results.
"I'm a little surprised at the level of interest in Baan," a broker said. "But it looks to have become a real favourite."
Philips also picked up support from a bouyant technology sector, rising 2.90 guilders and topping the volume list.
The decision to close loss-making home entertainment chain Superclub had helped convince investors the company was serious about cutting its unprofitable "bleeder" units, one dealer said.
Of the mid-caps, window coverings maker Hunter Douglas continued to benefit from a recommendation from NatWest as an outperformer in 1997, rising 5.50 guilders to 125.50.
Construction firm Volker Stevin also gained, with analysts pegging the shares as undervalued. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
